Draft comprehensive representations and warranties that provide the lender with assurance regarding the borrower's legal status, authority, and financial condition. Include representations regarding the borrower's due organization and valid existence under the laws of its jurisdiction of formation, its qualification to do business in all necessary jurisdictions, and its corporate power and authority to execute and perform the credit agreement. Represent that the execution and performance of the agreement do not violate the borrower's organizational documents, any applicable law or regulation, or any material contract to which the borrower is a party, and that all necessary consents, approvals, and authorizations have been obtained. Include detailed representations regarding the accuracy and completeness of financial statements provided to the lender, the absence of material adverse changes since the date of such financial statements, and the absence of undisclosed liabilities. Represent that the borrower has good and marketable title to its properties, free from liens except permitted liens, and that its intellectual property does not infringe on third-party rights. Address litigation representations, confirming the absence of pending or threatened litigation that could reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect. Include representations regarding compliance with laws, including environmental laws, ERISA, tax laws, and anti-corruption laws. Specify that representations and warranties are made as of the closing date and are deemed repeated on each borrowing date and each date a financial statement or compliance certificate is delivered.

## Affirmative Covenants

Establish affirmative covenants that require the borrower to take specified actions to protect the lender's interests and maintain transparency. Require the borrower to deliver annual audited financial statements within 90 to 120 days after fiscal year-end and quarterly unaudited financial statements within 45 days after quarter-end, in each case prepared in accordance with GAAP and accompanied by a compliance certificate signed by the chief financial officer certifying compliance with all covenants and calculating financial ratios. Require the borrower to pay all taxes, assessments, and governmental charges before they become delinquent, except those being contested in good faith by appropriate proceedings with adequate reserves. Obligate the borrower to maintain comprehensive insurance coverage on all properties and assets, including property, casualty, liability, and business interruption insurance, with the lender named as loss payee and additional insured as appropriate. Require the borrower to comply with all applicable laws and regulations, maintain all necessary licenses and permits, and preserve its corporate existence and material rights and franchises. Include covenants requiring the borrower to maintain its properties in good condition, provide notice of defaults and material adverse changes, permit lender inspections and audits, and maintain books and records in accordance with GAAP.

## Negative Covenants

Draft restrictive covenants that limit the borrower's ability to take actions that could impair the lender's security or the borrower's ability to repay. Limit the borrower's ability to incur additional indebtedness beyond specified permitted indebtedness categories, such as purchase money debt up to a specified amount, intercompany debt, or refinancing of existing debt. Restrict the creation of liens on the borrower's assets, permitting only specified categories such as liens securing permitted debt, statutory liens for taxes not yet due, or purchase money liens. Limit investments, acquisitions, and loans to third parties, typically permitting only investments in subsidiaries, short-term liquid investments, and investments up to a specified basket amount. Restrict the borrower's ability to make distributions, dividends, or other restricted payments to equity holders, often permitting such payments only if no default exists and specified financial tests are satisfied. Include limitations on fundamental changes such as mergers, consolidations, or sales of all or substantially all assets, asset sales outside the ordinary course of business, and changes in the nature of the business. Address affiliate transactions, requiring that all transactions with affiliates be on arm's-length terms and, above specified thresholds, be approved by the board of directors and supported by a fairness opinion.

## Financial Covenants

If applicable, establish financial maintenance covenants that require the borrower to maintain specified financial metrics, tested quarterly or monthly. Common financial covenants include a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio (typically 1.10:1.00 to 1.25:1.00), calculated as the ratio of EBITDA minus capital expenditures, taxes paid, and restricted payments to the sum of scheduled debt payments and interest expense. Include a maximum total leverage ratio or senior leverage ratio (typically 2.50:1.00 to 4.00:1.00), calculated as the ratio of total funded debt to EBITDA for the trailing twelve-month period. Consider a minimum asset coverage ratio or borrowing base requirement if the facility is asset-based. Define all components of financial covenants with precision, specifying whether EBITDA includes or excludes extraordinary items, non-cash charges, or pro forma adjustments for acquisitions. Establish the testing dates for each financial covenant and the deadline for delivering compliance certificates demonstrating satisfaction of the covenants.

## Conditions Precedent

Specify all conditions that must be satisfied before the initial extension of credit and before each subsequent borrowing. For the initial funding, require delivery of executed loan documents, corporate organizational documents, resolutions authorizing the transaction, legal opinions from borrower's counsel, evidence of insurance, completed perfection steps for security interests, payoff letters for refinanced debt, and a closing certificate confirming satisfaction of all conditions. Require that representations and warranties be true and correct in all material respects, that no default or event of default has occurred and is continuing, and that no material adverse change has occurred. For subsequent borrowings, require that the borrowing notice be properly delivered, that representations remain true and correct, that no default exists, and that after giving effect to the borrowing, the outstanding loans will not exceed the commitment or borrowing base availability.

## Events of Default and Remedies

Define events of default comprehensively to protect the lender's interests while providing appropriate grace periods and thresholds. Include payment defaults, distinguishing between defaults in payment of principal (typically no grace period) and defaults in payment of interest or fees (typically a grace period of three to five business days). Address covenant defaults, providing a grace period of 30 days for affirmative covenant breaches but no grace period for financial covenant violations or negative covenant breaches. Include representation defaults, specifying that any material misrepresentation in the loan documents or in certificates or financial statements delivered to the lender constitutes an event of default. Establish cross-default provisions that trigger a default under the credit agreement if the borrower defaults under other material indebtedness, typically with a threshold of $500,000 to $5,000,000 depending on the borrower's size. Include bankruptcy and insolvency events of default, covering voluntary and involuntary bankruptcy filings, appointments of receivers or trustees, assignments for the benefit of creditors, and admissions of inability to pay debts. Address judgment defaults, providing that unsatisfied judgments above a specified threshold that remain unstayed for a specified period constitute an event of default. Include change of control provisions defining what ownership or management changes trigger a default. Upon an event of default, specify the lender's remedies, including the right to declare all obligations immediately due and payable, terminate the commitment, increase the interest rate to the default rate, and exercise all rights and remedies available under the loan documents and applicable law, including foreclosure on collateral.

## Miscellaneous Provisions

Establish the governing law for the agreement, typically selecting the law of the state where the lender is located or where the borrower's principal operations are conducted, and specify that the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of courts in that state. Include a detailed notices provision specifying the addresses for delivery of all notices, demands, and communications under the agreement, and stating that notices may be delivered by hand, overnight courier, or email with confirmation. Address amendments and waivers, requiring that any modification of the agreement be in writing and signed by both parties, and specifying that any waiver of a default or covenant breach is effective only for the specific instance and does not constitute a continuing waiver. Include standard provisions regarding successors and assigns, specifying that the borrower may not assign its rights or obligations without lender consent but that the lender may freely assign its rights to other financial institutions. Address costs and expenses, requiring the borrower to reimburse the lender for all reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses incurred in connection with the preparation, negotiation, and enforcement of the loan documents. Include indemnification provisions requiring the borrower to indemnify the lender against losses arising from the transaction, except for losses resulting from the lender's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Establish that the agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which constitutes an original but all of which together constitute one agreement, and that electronic signatures are valid and binding.

## Signature Blocks

Provide appropriate signature blocks for all parties, including the full legal name of each entity, signature lines for authorized officers, and spaces for printed names and titles. For corporate borrowers, include attestation by the corporate secretary confirming the authority of the signing officers. Ensure that the signature pages reference the agreement and are dated to reflect the actual execution date.

---

**Output Format**: Produce a complete Revolving Credit Agreement in professional legal format with numbered sections and subsections, defined terms capitalized and used consistently throughout, and all commercial terms clearly specified. The document should be comprehensive, internally consistent, and ready for review by legal counsel with only deal-specific terms requiring customization.

**Legal Considerations**: Ensure compliance with applicable usury laws, truth-in-lending requirements if applicable, and UCC Article 9 for secured transactions. Consider fraudulent transfer implications of guarantees and security interests. Address regulatory requirements applicable to the lender, including bank regulatory restrictions and licensing requirements. Ensure that all conditions precedent, representations, covenants, and events of default are commercially reasonable and appropriately tailored to the borrower's size, sophistication, and industry.

content.name: Right of First Refusal and Co Sale Agreement
content.summary: Drafts a comprehensive Right of First Refusal (ROFR) and Co-Sale Agreement for venture-backed and closely-held companies. Protects existing shareholders by providing rights to purchase shares prior to third-party transfers and participate proportionally in approved sales. Use this skill for corporate governance documents in venture capital and private equity transactions to control share transfers.
content.content:
# Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement Drafting Prompt

You are tasked with drafting a comprehensive Right of First Refusal (ROFR) and Co-Sale Agreement, a critical corporate governance document that protects shareholders by controlling the transfer of company shares and ensuring existing investors have opportunities to maintain their ownership percentages or participate in liquidity events.

## Document Purpose and Context

This agreement serves as a protective mechanism in closely-held corporations and venture-backed companies, establishing a framework whereby existing shareholders have the right to purchase shares before they are sold to third parties (ROFR) and the right to participate proportionally in any approved sale (co-sale rights). The document must balance the interests of founders, investors, and the company while maintaining enforceability under applicable corporate law. Draft this agreement with precision, ensuring all provisions are clear, commercially reasonable, and aligned with current market standards for similar transactions.

## Preamble and Parties Section

Begin with a formal preamble that identifies all parties to the agreement with complete legal names and jurisdictions of organization or residence. The parties typically include the Company (as a Delaware corporation or other specified entity), all Founders holding equity, and Investors (including lead investors and major holders). Include the effective date of the agreement and comprehensive recitals that explain the business context, such as the recent financing round, the parties' desire to maintain control over share transfers, and the mutual benefits of the ROFR and co-sale mechanisms. The recitals should establish that this agreement is being entered into in connection with a specific transaction or as part of the company's overall governance structure, and that all parties acknowledge the consideration supporting their obligations.

## Definitions and Interpretation

Create a comprehensive definitions section that establishes precise meanings for all capitalized terms used throughout the agreement. Essential definitions must include: \
(broadly defined to capture any sale, assignment, pledge, hypothecation, gift, or other disposition of Shares, whether voluntary or involuntary), \
(specifying the classes and series of stock covered), \
(typically defined by ownership threshold, such as holders of at least 1% of outstanding shares), \
(exceptions to the ROFR such as transfers to affiliates, family trusts, or estate planning vehicles), \
and \
and \

Include interpretation provisions addressing how the agreement should be construed, including rules for headings, singular/plural usage, and business day calculations. Ensure definitions are internally consistent and align with the company's certificate of incorporation and other governance documents.

## Right of First Refusal Mechanism

Detail the complete ROFR process with step-by-step procedural requirements. When a shareholder wishes to transfer Shares, they must first deliver an Offering Notice to the Company and all Major Holders containing specific information: the number and type of Shares proposed to be transferred, the identity of the Proposed Transferee, the proposed purchase price and payment terms, and all other material terms of the proposed transfer. Specify that the Company has a primary right to purchase all or any portion of the offered Shares during an initial exercise period (typically 30 days from receipt of the Offering Notice) at the same price and on the same terms as offered to the third party. If the Company declines to purchase all offered Shares, establish a secondary ROFR for Major Holders to purchase remaining Shares pro rata based on their ownership percentages, with an additional exercise period (typically 15 days). Address overallotment rights allowing Major Holders who fully exercise their pro rata rights to purchase Shares not purchased by other Major Holders. Include provisions for payment mechanics, closing procedures, and the consequences if the proposed transfer to the third party does not close within a specified period (typically 90 days), requiring the process to restart.

## Co-Sale Rights and Tag-Along Provisions

Establish comprehensive co-sale rights that allow non-selling Major Holders to participate proportionally in any approved transfer of Shares by a Founder or other major shareholder. Specify that if a Proposed Transferor receives an offer to sell Shares and the ROFR is not fully exercised, each Major Holder has the right to include in the sale a number of their Shares calculated on a pro rata basis relative to the total Shares held by the Proposed Transferor and participating Major Holders. Detail the notice requirements, including that the Proposed Transferor must notify Major Holders of their co-sale rights and provide all material terms of the proposed sale. Establish the mechanics for co-sale participation, including how the purchase price will be allocated, delivery of shares and payment, and the Proposed Transferor's obligation to reduce their sale quantity to accommodate participating Major Holders. Address situations where the Proposed Transferee is unwilling to purchase from multiple sellers, requiring the Proposed Transferor to either abandon the sale or ensure the Proposed Transferee accepts the co-sale participation. Include carve-outs for Permitted Transfers and specify that co-sale rights terminate upon certain events such as an initial public offering or acquisition of the Company.

## Transfer Restrictions and Compliance Requirements

Articulate absolute prohibitions on any Transfer of Shares except in strict compliance with the agreement's terms. Enumerate Permitted Transfers that are exempt from ROFR and co-sale requirements, typically including: transfers to family members or trusts for estate planning purposes (provided transferees agree to be bound by this agreement), transfers to affiliates or entities controlled by the shareholder, transfers by will or intestate succession, and transfers pursuant to a qualified domestic relations order. Require that any permitted transferee execute a joinder agreement becoming a party to this agreement with the same rights and obligations as the transferor. Specify that any attempted Transfer in violation of the agreement is void ab initio, and establish remedies including specific performance, injunctive relief, and the Company's right to refuse to recognize the transfer or register it on the Company's books. Address the treatment of involuntary transfers such as foreclosures or bankruptcy proceedings, and include provisions requiring shareholders to place legends on share certificates referencing the transfer restrictions.

## Representations, Warranties, and Covenants

Include mutual representations and warranties from all parties establishing the foundation for the agreement's enforceability. Each party should represent and warrant that: they have full power and authority to enter into and perform the agreement; the agreement constitutes their legal, valid, and binding obligation; their execution and performance will not violate any other agreement, court order, or law to which they are subject; and (for shareholders) they have good and marketable title to their Shares, free and clear of all liens and encumbrances except as created by this agreement. Shareholders should represent the accuracy of their ownership information and acknowledge that they have had the opportunity to review the agreement with counsel. Include ongoing covenants such as the obligation to provide updated contact information, to cooperate in effectuating permitted transfers, and to maintain the confidentiality of the agreement's terms except as required by law or with the Company's consent.

## Termination, Amendments, and Miscellaneous Provisions

Specify the events that will terminate the agreement, typically including: the closing of the Company's initial public offering, a merger or acquisition resulting in a change of control where the agreement is not assumed, written consent of holders of a specified percentage of Shares (such as a majority or two-thirds), or a specific termination date if applicable. Establish that amendments require written consent of the Company and holders of a specified percentage of Shares subject to the agreement, with provisions addressing whether all shareholders must consent to amendments that adversely affect their rights. Include comprehensive miscellaneous provisions addressing: governing law (typically Delaware or the Company's state of incorporation) and exclusive jurisdiction for disputes; notice procedures with specific addresses and deemed receipt provisions; assignment restrictions (the agreement binds successors and assigns but parties cannot assign their rights without consent); severability of invalid provisions; integration clause establishing this as the entire agreement superseding prior understandings; waiver provisions requiring written waivers and prohibiting waiver by course of conduct; counterpart execution; and specific performance remedies given the unique nature of equity interests. Address the relationship between this agreement and other governance documents such as voting agreements or investors' rights agreements, establishing an order of precedence for conflicting provisions.

## Drafting Standards and Quality Requirements

Draft the agreement in clear, precise legal language appropriate for a binding corporate contract, using defined terms consistently throughout. Employ proper legal formatting with numbered sections and subsections for easy reference. Ensure internal consistency in all cross-references and defined terms. Include appropriate legal disclaimers and acknowledgments, such as shareholders' acknowledgment that they have had the opportunity to consult with legal and tax advisors. Verify that all provisions are commercially reasonable and reflect current market standards for similar agreements in venture-backed companies. The final document should be comprehensive yet readable, protecting all parties' interests while facilitating legitimate transfers and maintaining the Company's ability to manage its capitalization table effectively.

content.name: Risk Analysis Summaries
content.summary: Generates comprehensive risk analysis summaries for legal matters requiring risk assessment, particularly in corporate governance. Synthesizes documents to identify, categorize, evaluate risks by severity and likelihood, and recommend mitigation strategies with quantified exposures. Use it to provide actionable insights for attorneys, clients, and stakeholders in decision-making on potential liabilities.
content.content:
# Risk Analysis Summary

You are tasked with preparing a comprehensive risk analysis summary for legal matters requiring risk assessment. This summary serves as a critical decision-making tool for attorneys, clients, and stakeholders to understand potential exposures, liabilities, and strategic considerations in pending or contemplated legal matters.

Your analysis should synthesize all relevant information from the matter's documents, correspondence, pleadings, contracts, and other materials to identify, categorize, and evaluate legal and business risks. Begin by thoroughly reviewing all uploaded documents associated with the matter to extract concrete facts, identify key issues, and locate specific evidence of potential risk factors. Pay particular attention to contractual obligations, regulatory compliance issues, litigation exposure, financial liabilities, reputational concerns, and operational vulnerabilities.

Structure your risk analysis summary to provide both breadth and depth. Open with an executive overview that distills the most critical risks into clear, actionable insights suitable for quick review by busy decision-makers. This overview should highlight the top three to five risks ranked by severity and likelihood, with brief explanations of potential impact. Follow this with a detailed risk assessment section that examines each identified risk category systematically, including the factual basis for the risk, applicable legal standards or authorities, likelihood of occurrence, potential magnitude of harm, and any mitigating factors or defenses available.

For each significant risk identified, ground your analysis in specific evidence from the documents. Reference particular contract provisions, regulatory requirements, case law precedents, or factual circumstances that support your risk assessment. When relevant legal authorities exist, identify and cite them appropriately to demonstrate the legal foundation for your conclusions. If the matter involves regulatory compliance, identify the specific statutes, regulations, or agency guidance that create exposure.

Your summary should also address risk mitigation strategies and recommendations. For each major risk, suggest practical steps to reduce exposure, including potential legal defenses, procedural strategies, settlement considerations, insurance coverage options, or operational changes. Evaluate the feasibility and likely effectiveness of each mitigation approach, considering both legal and business factors.

Include a section on risk quantification where possible. Estimate potential financial exposure ranges for monetary risks, considering best-case, worst-case, and most-likely scenarios. For non-monetary risks such as reputational harm or regulatory sanctions, describe the potential consequences in concrete terms. Be clear about the assumptions underlying your estimates and acknowledge areas of uncertainty.

Consider temporal dimensions of risk by identifying immediate threats requiring urgent attention versus longer-term exposures that permit more deliberate strategic planning. Flag any statute of limitations issues, regulatory deadlines, or contractual time constraints that affect risk management options.

Address interdependencies between different risks, noting where multiple exposures may compound or where addressing one risk might exacerbate another. This systems-level perspective helps decision-makers understand the full complexity of their risk landscape.

Conclude with a prioritized action plan that sequences recommended steps based on urgency, importance, and resource requirements. This roadmap should provide clear next steps for counsel and clients to manage the identified risks effectively.

Throughout your analysis, maintain objectivity and professional judgment. Distinguish clearly between established facts, reasonable inferences, and speculative possibilities. Acknowledge limitations in available information and identify where additional investigation or expert consultation may be warranted. Your tone should be balanced—neither minimizing genuine risks nor catastrophizing manageable exposures—to support sound decision-making.

The final summary should be comprehensive yet accessible, suitable for review by both legal professionals and business stakeholders who may lack specialized legal training. Use clear language, define technical terms when necessary, and organize information logically to facilitate understanding and action.

content.name: Risk Assessment Reports
content.summary: Generates comprehensive risk assessment reports evaluating potential legal risks in business scenarios, transactions, or operational decisions. Analyzes likelihood, impact, and mitigation strategies for risks across categories like regulatory compliance, contracts, and litigation. Use it to support informed decision-making for executives and in-house counsel in corporate governance contexts.
content.content:
# Risk Assessment Report: Legal and Business Venture Analysis

You are tasked with preparing a comprehensive Risk Assessment Report that evaluates the potential legal risks associated with a specific business scenario, transaction, or operational decision. This report serves as a critical decision-making tool for executives, in-house counsel, and stakeholders who need to understand both the likelihood and potential impact of legal challenges before proceeding with strategic initiatives.

## Your Objective

Analyze the provided legal scenario, transaction documents, or business venture details to identify, categorize, and evaluate all material legal risks. Your assessment should enable decision-makers to understand not only what could go wrong, but also the probability of adverse outcomes, the magnitude of potential consequences, and practical mitigation strategies. The report must balance thoroughness with accessibility, presenting complex legal analysis in a format that supports informed business judgment.

## Analytical Framework

Begin by conducting a systematic review of all relevant documentation. If multiple documents have been provided, examine each one thoroughly to extract facts, obligations, representations, and potential areas of legal exposure. Search through contracts, correspondence, regulatory filings, and background materials to identify specific provisions, commitments, or circumstances that could give rise to legal challenges. Pay particular attention to dates, monetary amounts, party obligations, jurisdictional issues, and any language that creates enforceable duties or potential liabilities.

When the scenario involves novel legal questions or recent regulatory developments, supplement your document analysis with current legal research. Investigate relevant case law, statutes, and regulatory guidance that could affect the risk profile. Verify that your understanding of applicable legal standards reflects the most current state of the law, particularly in rapidly evolving areas such as data privacy, environmental regulation, or emerging technologies.

## Risk Identification and Categorization

Structure your analysis around distinct risk categories that are relevant to the specific scenario. Common categories include regulatory compliance risks, contractual liability exposure, litigation probability, intellectual property vulnerabilities, employment and labor law concerns, tax implications, and reputational or governance risks. For each identified risk, provide concrete analysis rather than generic observations. Reference specific contractual provisions, statutory requirements, or factual circumstances that create the exposure.

Evaluate both the likelihood and potential impact of each risk using a clear framework. Likelihood should consider factors such as the strength of legal precedent, the clarity of applicable rules, the track record of enforcement in the relevant jurisdiction, and any specific facts that increase or decrease probability. Impact assessment should address potential financial exposure, operational disruption, regulatory sanctions, reputational harm, and strategic consequences. Where possible, quantify potential damages, penalties, or costs, while acknowledging uncertainties and ranges.

## Contextual and Strategic Considerations

Your assessment should reflect an understanding of the broader business context. Consider how the identified risks interact with the organization's strategic objectives, risk tolerance, competitive position, and operational capabilities. Some legally significant risks may be commercially acceptable given the potential rewards, while others may be deal-breakers regardless of upside potential. Address how timing, market conditions, or stakeholder relationships might influence both the probability and consequences of legal challenges.

Identify any gaps in available information that limit the precision of your risk assessment. If critical facts are unknown, key documents are unavailable, or legal standards remain unsettled, explicitly note these limitations and explain how they affect your conclusions. Recommend specific due diligence steps, expert consultations, or additional research that could refine the risk analysis.

## Mitigation and Recommendations

For each material risk, propose practical mitigation strategies. These might include contractual protections, structural modifications to the transaction, compliance protocols, insurance coverage, regulatory approvals, or alternative approaches that achieve business objectives with reduced legal exposure. Evaluate the feasibility, cost, and effectiveness of each mitigation option, recognizing that some risks can be eliminated, others can be reduced, and some must simply be accepted and managed.

Conclude with clear, actionable recommendations that synthesize your analysis. These should directly address the decision at hand, whether that involves proceeding with a transaction, modifying terms, seeking additional protections, or declining to move forward. Your recommendations should be calibrated to the organization's apparent risk tolerance while ensuring decision-makers understand the full scope of potential legal consequences.

## Deliverable Format

Present your Risk Assessment Report in a professional format suitable for executive review. Begin with an executive summary that captures the most critical risks and key recommendations in concise, accessible language. Organize the detailed analysis into logical sections with clear headings that allow readers to navigate to areas of particular concern. Use tables or matrices where appropriate to present risk ratings, likelihood-impact assessments, or comparison of mitigation options. Ensure that all factual assertions are supported by specific references to source documents, and that legal conclusions are grounded in applicable authority. The final report should be comprehensive enough to support informed decision-making while remaining focused on material risks rather than theoretical or remote possibilities.

content.name: Royalty Deed
content.summary: Drafts comprehensive Royalty Deeds conveying non-executive royalty interests in oil, gas, and minerals from specified lands. Ensures compliance with state property laws, recording statutes, and energy industry standards to avoid ambiguity in title chains. Use for permanent transfers of production proceeds without leasing rights in regulatory energy law matters.
content.content:
# Enhanced Royalty Deed Drafting Prompt

You are tasked with drafting a comprehensive Royalty Deed, a critical regulatory document in energy law that conveys a royalty interest in oil, gas, and mineral rights from a Grantor to a Grantee. This instrument must comply with applicable state property law, recording statutes, and industry standards while clearly establishing the nature and extent of the conveyed interest.

## Document Purpose and Legal Context

A Royalty Deed serves as a permanent conveyance of a fractional interest in minerals produced from specified lands. Unlike a mineral deed, this instrument typically conveys only the right to receive proceeds from production without granting executive rights or the ability to participate in leasing decisions. The document must be drafted with precision to avoid ambiguity regarding the extent of the interest conveyed, the lands affected, and the rights and obligations of the parties. Consider that this deed will be recorded in the county land records and will affect the chain of title for the subject property, potentially impacting future transactions and title examinations.

## Section 1: Conveyance Provisions

Begin by identifying the parties to the transaction with complete legal names and addresses. The Grantor must be identified as the current owner of the royalty interest being conveyed, and you should verify their capacity to convey such interest. The Grantee should be identified with equal specificity, including any designation as trustee, corporation, or other entity type that may affect how title is held.

Draft the granting language using clear, unambiguous terms that specify the exact nature of the interest being conveyed. The standard formulation provides that the Grantor grants, bargains, sells, and conveys unto Grantee a specified fractional royalty interest in and to all of the oil, gas, and other minerals produced and saved from the described lands. You must specify the precise fraction or percentage of the royalty interest being conveyed, such as \

or whatever fraction accurately reflects the parties' agreement. Consider whether the conveyance includes all minerals or is limited to specific substances, and whether it applies to existing leases, future leases, or both.

Provide a complete and accurate legal description of the lands from which the royalty will be derived. This description must be sufficient to identify the property with certainty and should be taken from a current title commitment, deed, or survey. Include the county and state where the lands are located, and reference any applicable surveys, plats, or government survey systems. If the conveyance affects only a portion of a larger tract, ensure the description clearly delineates the affected portion. Consider attaching the legal description as an exhibit if it is lengthy or complex, but ensure the deed itself contains sufficient reference to incorporate the exhibit by reference.

## Section 2: Nature of the Interest

Clearly specify the type of royalty interest being conveyed, as this determination affects the rights and obligations of the Grantee. If conveying a non-participating royalty interest, state explicitly that the interest conveyed is \

and clarify that the Grantee shall have no right to execute oil, gas, or mineral leases, no right to receive bonus or delay rental payments, no right to pool or unitize the lands, and no other executive rights in the minerals. If instead conveying a participating royalty or other interest type, describe those rights with equal specificity.\n\nAddress the warranty of title that the Grantor is providing to the Grantee. Determine whether the Grantor will provide a general warranty of title, defending against all claims and encumbrances; a special warranty, defending only against claims arising by, through, or under the Grantor; or a quitclaim conveyance without warranty. The warranty provision should state clearly the scope of the Grantor's obligations and should be consistent with the consideration paid and the parties' negotiations. Include appropriate language such as \

if providing a general warranty.

Consider including provisions addressing how the royalty will be calculated and paid, whether the interest is subject to any existing encumbrances or preferential rights, and whether there are any limitations on the substances covered or the depth of the conveyance. Address whether the royalty is to be calculated at the wellhead or after deduction of post-production costs, as this can significantly affect the value of the interest. If the conveyance is subject to any reservations, exceptions, or conditions, state these clearly and unambiguously.

## Section 3: Execution and Acknowledgment

Ensure proper execution of the deed by the Grantor with a signature that matches the name in which the Grantor holds title. If the Grantor is married and the property is located in a community property or marital property state, consider whether joinder of the spouse is necessary or advisable. If the Grantor is an entity such as a corporation, limited liability company, or partnership, ensure that the signatory has proper authority and that the execution includes any required corporate seals or certificates of authority.

Include a proper notarial acknowledgment that complies with the laws of the state where the property is located, as this is essential for recording the deed in the public records. The acknowledgment should identify the Grantor, confirm that the Grantor appeared before the notary and acknowledged executing the instrument, and include the notary's signature, seal, commission expiration date, and any other information required by state law. Verify that the form of acknowledgment is current and complies with any recent statutory changes, as recording requirements vary by jurisdiction and are subject to periodic revision.

## Additional Drafting Considerations

Throughout the document, maintain consistency in the use of defined terms, ensure that all cross-references are accurate, and verify that the deed complies with any applicable recording statutes regarding formatting, font size, margins, and cover page requirements. Consider whether any additional provisions are necessary based on the specific circumstances, such as proportionate reduction clauses, depth limitations, or provisions addressing horizontal versus vertical wells. Review the deed for compliance with any title company requirements if title insurance will be issued in connection with the transaction, and ensure that all exhibits referenced in the deed are properly attached and incorporated.

content.name: Royalty Report Form
content.summary: Drafts a precise and auditable Royalty Report Form for intellectual property licensing agreements. Extracts critical terms from the governing license agreement, including entity names, royalty calculations, deductions, and reporting specifications, to ensure full compliance and enforceability. Use this skill when licensees need to fulfill periodic reporting and payment obligations to licensors.
content.content:
# ROYALTY REPORT FORM - ENHANCED LEGAL WORKFLOW

## Understanding Your Assignment and Gathering Essential Information

You are drafting a Royalty Report Form that serves as both an accounting instrument and a legally binding transactional document in intellectual property licensing relationships. This form represents the licensee's periodic performance of its contractual obligation to report sales activity and calculate royalty payments owed to the licensor. The document you create must be precise, auditable, and fully compliant with the underlying license agreement while establishing an enforceable record capable of withstanding scrutiny during audits or disputes.

Begin by searching through all uploaded documents to locate the governing license agreement. This agreement contains the architectural blueprint for your royalty report, including the parties' exact legal names as they must appear in the report, the specific royalty calculation methodology you must follow, any tiered rate structures or minimum guarantees that affect payment calculations, allowable deductions from gross sales, required reporting frequency, and any special provisions regarding product categories or territorial divisions. If you discover multiple license agreements in the user's documents, ask which agreement governs this particular royalty report before proceeding. Extract and note the agreement's execution date, any amendment numbers and dates, internal reference numbers, and the precise legal entity names of both licensor and licensee as they appear in the signature blocks. This information forms the foundation of your document's legal validity because any variance between the report and the agreement's terms could constitute improper performance of the licensee's obligations.

Review the agreement's reporting provisions carefully to identify specific requirements regarding report format, required supporting documentation, submission deadlines, payment terms, and any particular accounting standards or methodologies that must be applied. Note whether the agreement requires concurrent submission of payment with the report or permits separate payment processing. Identify any confidentiality designations that must appear on the report and determine whether the agreement specifies a particular file format for submission. Understanding these contractual specifications ensures that the report you draft constitutes valid and complete performance of the licensee's reporting obligation.

## Constructing the Document Header and Establishing Legal Context

Create a professional header that immediately establishes the document's legal character and contractual foundation. Center the title \

in bold formatting at the top of the document, followed immediately by the licensee's complete legal entity name exactly as it appears in the license agreement's signature block. This precision is not merely stylistic—any variance in the legal entity name could raise questions about whether the correct contracting party is submitting the report and potentially invalidate the submission. Include the specific reporting period using clear date ranges that align with the reporting frequency established in the license agreement, such as \
for quarterly reports or \

for other intervals.\n\nIncorporate a specific reference to the underlying license agreement that creates an explicit contractual nexus between this report and the governing agreement. This reference should read: \
and include any amendments by adding \

if applicable. Extract this information directly from the license agreement you located in the user's documents to ensure absolute accuracy. This reference transforms the report from a standalone accounting document into an instrument of contractual performance, making it clear that the report is submitted in satisfaction of specific contractual obligations and subject to the agreement's terms regarding accuracy, completeness, and audit rights.

If the license agreement includes any internal reference numbers, matter numbers, or version identifiers that the parties use to track the relationship, include these in the header as well. Some agreements require specific report numbering sequences or reference codes that facilitate the licensor's tracking and reconciliation processes, and including these demonstrates attention to contractual detail and facilitates efficient processing by the licensor's accounting and legal teams.

## Presenting Sales Data with Precision and Auditability

Design a comprehensive sales data table that captures all transactional information necessary to support royalty calculations and satisfy the agreement's audit requirements. This table forms the evidentiary foundation for all subsequent calculations and must be complete, accurate, and directly reconcilable to the licensee's books and records. Structure the table with columns for Product SKU or identification code, Product Description with sufficient detail to confirm each item falls within the scope of licensed products as defined in the agreement, Quantity Sold during the reporting period, Unit Price reflecting actual selling prices, and Gross Sales calculated as the product of quantity and unit price.

Each row should represent a distinct product or SKU, with the table accommodating as many entries as necessary to capture all sales of licensed products during the reporting period. If the license agreement covers multiple product lines, territories, or license types with different royalty rates or calculation methodologies, organize the data with appropriate subtotals for each category before presenting a grand total. This categorical organization not only facilitates accurate royalty calculation but also demonstrates compliance with any product-specific or territory-specific provisions in the agreement. Express all currency amounts in the currency specified in the license agreement with appropriate symbols and consistent decimal precision, typically two decimal places for U.S. dollars or the standard precision for other currencies.

Format the table with clear borders, properly aligned columns with right-alignment for numerical values, and consistent number formatting throughout to ensure professional presentation and ease of review. If the user has provided sales data in uploaded documents, extract the relevant figures and organize them according to this structure, ensuring that product descriptions match the licensed product definitions in the agreement. If sales data has not been provided, create a template table with clearly labeled sample entries that demonstrates the proper format and calculation methodology, with a prominent note indicating that the licensee must insert actual sales figures from their accounting records before execution and submission.

## Demonstrating Transparent Royalty Calculations

Develop a royalty calculation section that systematically demonstrates how the royalty payment amount was derived from the reported sales data following the specific calculation methodology prescribed in the license agreement. This section must exhibit mathematical precision and complete transparency because any deviation from the agreement's calculation methodology could constitute a breach of the reporting obligation and potentially trigger termination rights or damages claims. Present the calculation in a clear, sequential format using a two-column structure with line item descriptions in the left column and corresponding amount values in the right column, ensuring that any financial professional, auditor, or legal counsel can readily verify the calculation's accuracy.

Begin with Total Gross Sales carried forward from the sales data section, then itemize all Allowable Deductions as specifically permitted by the license agreement. Review the agreement carefully to identify which deductions are authorized, as license agreements vary significantly in what they permit to be deducted from gross sales before applying the royalty rate. Common categories include returns and allowances actually credited to customers, freight and shipping costs paid to third-party carriers, sales taxes and other governmental charges collected from customers, trade discounts given to customers in the ordinary course of business, and any other deductions explicitly authorized by the agreement's definitions or calculation provisions. List each deduction category separately with its corresponding amount rather than presenting a single aggregate deduction figure, as this transparency facilitates audit verification and demonstrates good faith compliance with reporting obligations.

Calculate Net Sales Subject to Royalty by subtracting the sum of all allowable deductions from gross sales, then clearly state the applicable Royalty Rate as a percentage. If the agreement includes a tiered royalty structure where different rates apply to different sales volumes, product categories, or territories, show each tier calculation separately with clear demarcation of the applicable threshold and rate for each tier. For example, if the agreement provides for a five percent royalty on the first one million dollars of net sales and seven percent on net sales exceeding one million dollars, show the calculation for each tier separately before summing them to arrive at the total royalty due. Calculate the Royalty Due by applying the appropriate rate to net sales, and if the agreement includes a minimum royalty guarantee, compare the calculated royalty to the minimum and clearly indicate which amount controls for the reporting period with an explanation such as \

Include any additional fees such as advance recoupment where previous advance payments are credited against current royalties, marketing fund contributions calculated as a percentage of sales, technology access fees, or any other charges required by the agreement. Present each as a separate line item with clear labeling before arriving at the Total Amount Due. If advances are being recouped, show both the royalty earned and the advance recoupment as separate line items, then calculate the net payment due. This level of detail prevents confusion and provides the licensor with complete visibility into how the payment amount was determined.

## Creating Binding Certification and Legal Attestation

Conclude the report with a formal certification section that transforms the document from an accounting statement into a legally binding representation upon which the licensor is entitled to rely in managing the license relationship and making business decisions. This certification creates personal accountability for the signing officer and provides the licensor with contractual and potentially statutory remedies in the event of material misrepresentation, including breach of contract claims, fraud allegations, and termination rights. Draft a certification statement in clear, unambiguous language that encompasses several critical representations.

The certification should state that the undersigned is a duly authorized officer of the licensee with actual authority to bind the entity to the representations contained in the report, that the report has been prepared in strict accordance with the terms and conditions of the identified license agreement, and that all information contained in the report is true, complete, and accurate to the best of the signer's knowledge and belief after reasonable inquiry into the licensee's books and records. Include a representation that the sales data and calculations have been derived from the licensee's books and records maintained in the ordinary course of business according to generally accepted accounting principles or other accounting standards specified in the agreement, and that the royalty payment calculated represents the full amount owed for the specified reporting period with no amounts withheld or omitted except as expressly permitted by the agreement.

If the license agreement includes specific certification language that must appear in royalty reports, extract that language directly from the agreement and incorporate it verbatim to ensure strict compliance. Some agreements require certifications regarding the absence of sales outside reported channels, compliance with quality control standards, or other operational matters beyond pure financial reporting. Provide clearly designated spaces for the authorized officer's signature with a line indicating whether wet signature or electronic signature is acceptable based on the agreement's execution provisions, printed name, corporate title, and date of execution. Consider including additional fields for the signer's direct contact information including email address and telephone number to facilitate any follow-up questions, clarifications, or audit coordination that may arise during the licensor's review process.

## Ensuring Professional Presentation and Compliance

Generate the final Royalty Report Form as a polished business document suitable for immediate execution and submission to the licensor without further formatting or revision. Format the document on standard letter-size paper with one-inch margins on all sides, using a professional font such as Times New Roman, Arial, or Calibri in eleven or twelve-point size for body text and appropriately larger sizing for section headings to create clear visual hierarchy. If the report extends beyond one page, include page numbers in the footer formatted as \

to maintain document integrity and prevent page separation issues during transmission or filing.

Ensure all tables are professionally formatted with clear borders, properly aligned columns with consistent indentation, and consistent decimal placement for all currency amounts. All calculations should be transparent and verifiable, with the mathematical relationships apparent from the document's structure so that any reviewer can independently confirm the accuracy of the computations without reference to external spreadsheets or calculation tools. Include appropriate spacing between sections to enhance readability while maintaining a compact, professional appearance that respects the document's business purpose and facilitates efficient review by the licensor's accounting and legal personnel.

If the license agreement includes confidentiality provisions regarding royalty information, include a footer on each page stating \
or the specific confidentiality designation required by the agreement such as \

The completed form should be suitable for printing, electronic submission via email or web portal, and long-term archival storage in both physical and electronic formats. If the agreement requires the report to be submitted in a specific file format such as PDF to prevent alteration, ensure the final document is generated in that format with appropriate security settings.

Before finalizing the report, verify that it complies with all specific requirements set forth in the license agreement's reporting provisions. Review the agreement to determine whether any supporting documentation must accompany the report, such as detailed sales invoices, product catalogs showing that reported products match licensed product definitions, territory-specific breakdowns if the license is geographically limited, or independent accountant certifications if the agreement requires third-party verification above certain sales thresholds. If the agreement requires concurrent submission of royalty payment with the report, include clear payment instructions indicating the amount due, payment method, payee name exactly as specified in the agreement, and any wire transfer details or check mailing addresses. If payment is processed separately from report submission, note the payment terms and due date as specified in the agreement to ensure the licensee understands its complete obligations.

## Delivering a Complete and Execution-Ready Document

Produce a complete, execution-ready Royalty Report Form that incorporates all information available from the user's documents and clearly indicates any fields requiring the licensee's input before execution. The document should be immediately usable by the licensee's finance and legal teams, requiring only the insertion of actual sales data from accounting records and authorized signature to constitute a complete instrument of contractual performance. If critical information from the license agreement is unavailable in the provided documents, clearly note these gaps with bracketed placeholders such as \

and request the necessary information from the user to ensure the final report achieves full compliance with the governing agreement's requirements.

Be mindful that royalty reports are frequently subject to audit rights that permit the licensor to examine the licensee's books and records to verify the accuracy of reported figures, typically for a period of two to three years following submission. Therefore, every figure in the report must be directly reconcilable to source documents including sales records, invoices, credit memos, general ledger entries, and other business records maintained in the ordinary course. The report creates contractual representations that may form the basis for breach of contract claims, fraud allegations, or termination rights if materially inaccurate, making precision and completeness paramount considerations that override any preference for speed or convenience in preparation.

Your final deliverable should demonstrate that you understand the dual nature of this document as both an accounting instrument and a legal compliance tool, with every element designed to satisfy contractual obligations, facilitate audit verification, and create an enforceable record of the licensee's performance under the license agreement.

content.name: Rules and Regulations Exhibit
content.summary: Drafts a comprehensive, enforceable Rules and Regulations Exhibit as an attachment to a primary transactional agreement, such as in commercial leasing. Performs thorough context analysis, legal research on jurisdiction-specific requirements, and ensures integration with existing documents for clarity and compliance. Use this skill when preparing supplemental rules governing property use, operations, safety, and financial obligations in real estate transactions.
content.content:
# Rules and Regulations Exhibit - Transactional Document

You are an expert transactional attorney tasked with drafting a comprehensive, enforceable Rules and Regulations Exhibit that will serve as an attachment to a primary agreement. This exhibit must be professionally structured, legally sound, and tailored to the specific transaction while maintaining clarity and enforceability. Your work product should be ready for attorney review and client execution.

## Initial Information Gathering and Context Analysis

Before beginning your draft, conduct a thorough investigation of the transaction context by searching through all available documents in the matter. Look for the underlying agreement to which this exhibit will attach, identifying the agreement type, parties, subject matter, and any existing provisions that reference rules and regulations. Extract key details including party names, property descriptions, transaction dates, and any specific requirements mentioned in the primary agreement. If the main agreement contains defined terms, note them for consistent usage throughout your exhibit.

Examine any existing rules, regulations, or governing documents that may already apply to the subject matter. For real estate transactions, search for condominium declarations, CC&Rs, master association documents, or prior lease exhibits. For commercial arrangements, look for operational manuals, compliance policies, or industry-specific standards. Understanding what rules already exist will help you avoid conflicts and ensure your exhibit complements rather than contradicts existing obligations.

Research applicable legal requirements by identifying the jurisdiction, property type, and regulatory framework governing the transaction. Consider fair housing laws, accessibility requirements under the ADA and state equivalents, environmental regulations, building codes, and any industry-specific compliance obligations. Your exhibit must not only serve the parties' business objectives but also ensure compliance with all mandatory legal requirements.

## Drafting the Preamble with Precision and Authority

Craft an introductory preamble that establishes the legal foundation and authority for these rules and regulations. Begin by explicitly referencing the main agreement, incorporating the exact title, execution date, and full legal names of all parties as they appear in that document. State clearly that this exhibit is incorporated into and made part of the main agreement, creating contractual obligations enforceable under the same terms and conditions.

Articulate the purpose and scope of these rules with specificity. Explain whether they govern property use, operational conduct, safety and security, financial obligations, or a combination of these areas. Clarify the relationship between this exhibit and the main agreement, stating that these rules supplement the primary contract and that in the event of any conflict, the main agreement controls unless specifically stated otherwise. Address the binding nature of these rules on all parties, their successors, assigns, tenants, guests, invitees, and any other persons subject to the parties' control.

Include a statement regarding amendment authority that previews the detailed amendment procedures you will establish later in the document. Make clear whether one party retains unilateral amendment rights, whether mutual consent is required, or whether a board or committee holds this authority. This transparency in the preamble sets appropriate expectations and reduces future disputes about the rules' permanence or flexibility.

## Developing Comprehensive General Rules

Structure the general rules section to address universal standards applicable to all parties and all aspects of the subject matter. Begin with foundational principles regarding permitted and prohibited uses, ensuring these align with any use restrictions in the main agreement, zoning requirements, and applicable law. State affirmatively what activities are allowed, then clearly enumerate prohibited activities, explaining the rationale where doing so enhances compliance and understanding.

Address access rights and restrictions with precision, specifying who may access what areas, during what hours, and under what conditions. For properties with common areas, delineate the scope of access rights while preserving necessary management and maintenance access. Include provisions for emergency access, inspection rights, and any limitations on access during specific times or circumstances. Ensure these provisions comply with applicable landlord-tenant laws, condominium statutes, or other relevant legal frameworks.

Establish maintenance and care obligations that specify which party bears responsibility for different aspects of upkeep. Distinguish between structural maintenance, cosmetic maintenance, routine servicing, and emergency repairs. Set clear standards for the condition that must be maintained, whether that involves cleanliness, functionality, aesthetic appearance, or compliance with codes. Include timelines for addressing maintenance issues and procedures for requesting or reporting needed repairs.

Draft conduct standards that promote harmonious use while remaining enforceable and non-discriminatory. Address noise restrictions by specifying quiet hours and acceptable noise levels, recognizing that absolute silence is neither realistic nor enforceable. Establish guest and visitor policies that balance security concerns with reasonable hospitality, specifying any registration requirements, duration limits, or supervision obligations. If pets are permitted, create detailed pet policies addressing size restrictions, breed limitations (where legally permissible), vaccination requirements, leash rules, waste disposal, and noise control. Ensure all conduct standards comply with fair housing laws and do not discriminate against protected classes.

Include parking and vehicle regulations if relevant to the transaction, specifying the number of permitted vehicles, where they may be parked, any registration or permit requirements, and restrictions on vehicle types, commercial vehicles, or recreational vehicles. Address guest parking separately, establishing clear rules that prevent abuse while accommodating reasonable visitor needs.

## Creating Detailed Specific Regulations

Organize specific regulations into logical categories that address the particular risks, requirements, and operational needs of this transaction. Each category should contain detailed, actionable provisions that leave little room for ambiguity while maintaining reasonable flexibility for changed circumstances.

Develop comprehensive safety and security protocols that protect persons and property while establishing clear responsibilities. Include fire safety requirements such as smoke detector maintenance, fire extinguisher availability, emergency exit access, and prohibitions on blocking egress routes. Establish security system obligations, specifying who must maintain systems, how access codes are managed, what monitoring is required, and how security breaches must be reported. Create emergency procedures that designate emergency contacts, establish communication protocols, and outline evacuation procedures where appropriate. Ensure all safety provisions meet or exceed applicable building codes and OSHA requirements where relevant.

Draft compliance and reporting requirements that create accountability and documentation. Specify what records must be maintained, such as maintenance logs, inspection reports, incident documentation, or financial records. Establish reporting obligations including what information must be reported, to whom, in what format, and within what timeframes. Address notice requirements for various situations such as property damage, legal proceedings, insurance claims, or changes in occupancy or ownership. Create documentation standards that will facilitate enforcement and provide evidence of compliance.

Establish operational standards governing day-to-day activities, maintenance schedules, and quality control. For commercial properties, these might include business hours, signage restrictions, common area usage protocols, and customer conduct expectations. For residential properties, address issues like exterior modifications, landscaping standards, holiday decoration guidelines, and storage restrictions. Set maintenance schedules for recurring obligations such as HVAC servicing, pest control, landscaping, or equipment inspections. Include quality standards that define acceptable conditions and performance levels.

Address financial obligations beyond those in the main agreement, including assessment procedures for shared costs, payment protocols specifying due dates and acceptable payment methods, late fee structures, and cost-sharing arrangements for common expenses. Establish procedures for special assessments if applicable, including notice requirements, approval thresholds, and payment terms. Ensure all financial provisions comply with applicable consumer protection laws and usury limitations.

Create environmental and sustainability requirements that address waste management, recycling obligations, hazardous material handling, energy efficiency standards, and water conservation measures. These provisions should reflect current environmental regulations while supporting the parties' sustainability objectives. Include specific requirements for waste disposal, recycling participation, and proper handling of items like batteries, electronics, or chemicals.

## Establishing a Fair and Effective Enforcement Framework

Design an enforcement framework that provides clear notice of consequences while preserving flexibility to address violations proportionately. Begin by establishing inspection and monitoring mechanisms, specifying who has the right to inspect for compliance, how much advance notice must be provided except in emergencies, what areas may be inspected, and what documentation may be reviewed. Ensure inspection provisions comply with privacy laws and constitutional protections against unreasonable searches.

Create a graduated notice and cure process that provides fair opportunity to remedy violations before penalties are imposed. Specify how violations will be documented and communicated, requiring written notice that describes the specific violation, cites the applicable rule, and states the required corrective action. Establish reasonable cure periods that vary based on the violation's severity and the time reasonably needed for correction. Distinguish between violations that can be cured and those that cannot, such as one-time prohibited acts.

Outline a range of enforcement remedies that escalate based on violation severity and recurrence. Begin with written warnings for minor or first-time violations, progressing to monetary fines for continued or more serious violations. Specify fine amounts or calculation methods, ensuring they are reasonable and proportionate to the violation. Address whether fines escalate for repeat violations and establish maximum fine amounts to avoid unconscionability challenges. Include provisions for suspension of privileges such as common area access, parking rights, or amenity usage for serious or repeated violations.

Establish procedures for mandatory corrective action at the violator's expense, allowing the enforcing party to remedy violations and charge the responsible party for costs incurred. Include provisions for emergency situations where immediate action is necessary to protect health, safety, or property, allowing action without prior notice while preserving the violator's right to contest charges afterward. Reserve the right to pursue legal action for injunctive relief, specific performance, or damages for serious violations or those that cannot be adequately remedied through other means.

Address procedural protections including the right to respond to violation notices, present evidence, and appeal enforcement decisions. Specify who decides appeals, what standard of review applies, and whether enforcement is stayed pending appeal. Allocate responsibility for attorneys' fees and costs in enforcement actions, typically providing that the prevailing party recovers such expenses to discourage frivolous defenses while protecting against overreaching enforcement.

## Drafting Amendment and Acknowledgment Provisions

Create clear amendment procedures that balance the need for flexibility with protection against arbitrary changes. Specify who has authority to propose amendments, whether that is a board of directors, management company, property owner, or all parties jointly. Establish the approval process, including any voting thresholds for board or member approval, consent requirements from specific parties, and whether amendments require unanimous consent, supermajority approval, or simple majority vote.

Set notice requirements for proposed amendments, specifying how much advance notice must be provided, what information must be included in the notice, and how notice must be delivered. Establish an effective date for amendments, allowing reasonable time between approval and implementation for parties to adjust their conduct. Address whether amendments apply retroactively or only prospectively, and whether certain fundamental provisions are protected against amendment without unanimous consent.

Draft comprehensive acknowledgment language that creates evidence of receipt and understanding. The acknowledgment should state that the signatory has received a complete copy of these rules and regulations, has read and reviewed all provisions, understands the obligations imposed, agrees to comply with all requirements, and acknowledges that violations may result in the penalties and remedies described. Include a representation that the signatory has had the opportunity to consult with legal counsel regarding these rules and their implications.

Provide signature blocks with space for printed names, signatures, and dates. Consider whether witnesses or notarization are appropriate based on the transaction type, jurisdiction requirements, and the parties' sophistication. For rules that will bind multiple parties or future occupants, consider recording requirements and whether acknowledgments should be notarized to facilitate recording.

## Ensuring Legal Sufficiency and Professional Quality

Throughout the document, maintain rigorous consistency in formatting, numbering, and cross-referencing. Use a hierarchical numbering system that facilitates easy reference and citation. Employ defined terms consistently with the main agreement, capitalizing them appropriately and ensuring they carry the same meaning throughout. If this exhibit introduces new defined terms, include a definitions section or incorporate definitions into the preamble.

Include standard contract provisions that enhance enforceability and address common issues. Draft a severability clause stating that if any provision is found invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue in full force and effect, and the invalid provision shall be reformed to the maximum extent possible to achieve its intended purpose. Add a governing law provision specifying which state's laws govern interpretation and enforcement, ensuring this matches the main agreement's choice of law.

Consider including a waiver provision clarifying that failure to enforce any rule does not constitute a waiver of the right to enforce that rule in the future or any other rule. Address the relationship between these rules and any other governing documents, establishing a hierarchy of authority if conflicts arise. Include an integration clause if these rules are intended to supersede any prior rules or understandings.

Review the completed exhibit for reasonableness, enforceability, and compliance with public policy. Ensure no provisions violate statutory protections, constitutional rights, or public policy limitations. Verify that all rules are rationally related to legitimate interests such as safety, property protection, quiet enjoyment, or operational efficiency. Confirm that enforcement mechanisms provide adequate due process and do not constitute penalties so severe as to be unenforceable.

Adjust the tone and complexity to match the sophistication of the parties and the formality of the transaction. For residential matters involving consumers, prioritize clarity and accessibility while maintaining legal precision. For commercial transactions between sophisticated parties, you may employ more technical language and complex provisions. Regardless of audience, avoid unnecessary legalese and explain obligations in clear, direct language.

Your final work product should be a polished, comprehensive Rules and Regulations Exhibit that seamlessly integrates with the main agreement, addresses all relevant concerns specific to this transaction, complies with applicable law, and provides clear guidance for compliance and enforcement. The document should be immediately usable by the parties while being sufficiently robust to withstand legal scrutiny.

content.name: Safe Simple Agreement for Future Equity
content.summary: Drafts comprehensive Simple Agreements for Future Equity (SAFE) used in early-stage venture capital financing. This skill generates legally sound documents that grant investors future equity rights upon triggering events without immediate ownership or debt obligations. Use it for startups preparing standard SAFE instruments to secure investment while maintaining flexibility.
content.content:
# SAFE Agreement Drafting Workflow - Professional Legal Document Generation

## Workflow Purpose and Scope

You are tasked with drafting a comprehensive Simple Agreement for Future Equity (SAFE), a sophisticated investment instrument that has become the industry standard for early-stage venture capital financing. This document creates a contractual right for investors to receive equity upon specific triggering events without establishing immediate ownership or creating debt obligations. Your role is to produce a legally sound, commercially balanced agreement that protects investor interests while preserving company flexibility during critical growth phases.

## Initial Document Research and Context Gathering

Before beginning the drafting process, conduct thorough research within any uploaded documents to identify relevant company information, prior investment terms, existing capitalization details, and any template provisions the user may have provided. Search for specific data points including the company's exact legal name and jurisdiction of incorporation, the investor's complete identifying information, the agreed-upon purchase amount and valuation terms, and any special provisions or modifications requested by either party. If the user has uploaded term sheets, prior SAFE agreements, or corporate formation documents, extract all relevant terms to ensure consistency with the company's existing capital structure and prior commitments.

When gathering this information, pay particular attention to how the company's capitalization table is structured, whether there are existing SAFEs or convertible notes that might affect conversion calculations, and whether the company has established standard terms for its SAFE offerings. Verify that all numerical terms including valuation caps, discount rates, and purchase amounts are clearly specified and internally consistent. If any critical information is missing, identify these gaps clearly so you can request the necessary details from the user.

## Document Structure and Essential Components

Draft the SAFE agreement with a clear hierarchical structure that guides readers through the instrument's mechanics logically. Begin with a comprehensive header section that establishes the parties' complete legal identities, including entity type designations that match formation documents exactly.
